_comment: Copy to ~/.config/viewport/config.json, or pass --config PATH.
This is the tier that must keep working when the web shell does not.
The shell is fetched over the network; if it 404s, throws, or hangs,
anything it owned dies with it. Bindings defined here still work in
that state, which is the difference between a broken desktop UI and a
machine you cannot quit without switching to a TTY.
The shell may add more bindings at runtime with bind.add over IPC.
That layer is additive and expendable; keep exit and a terminal here.
Precedence: command-line flags > this file > built-in defaults.
Two ways to write keybindings, and this file demonstrates the heavier
one. Defining any "binds" object at all suppresses the built-in
defaults, so an empty one means 'no keybindings' — that is what it is
for, and it is why everything below has to be spelled out.
To change a few chords and keep the rest, use "binds_override"
instead. It is not shown here because there would be nothing to show:
"binds_override": { "Mod4+Return": "exec foot", "Mod4+d": null }
opens foot instead of the built-in terminal, lets Mod4+d through to the
focused application, and leaves every other default alone. A null (or
the action "none") unbinds a chord, which is not the same as leaving
it out: leaving it out is what asks for the built-in.
_layout: "tiling"   i3/sway: splits, plus tabbed and stacked containers.
"scrolling" niri: an endless strip of columns that scrolls to follow
focus. Opening a window never resizes the ones already
open. Changes the default movement bindings to match:
Mod4+h/l walk the strip, Mod4+j/k move inside a column,
Mod4+comma/period consume and expel, Mod4+r cycles the
column width.
"solar"     the focused window in the middle at 60% of the screen, the
rest in orbit around it — eight at full size in the margin,
the rest at the edges and corners drawn at 40% and dimmed.
Focus is what puts a window in the middle, so the one being
typed into is never shrunk, dimmed or covered. Mod4+h/j/k/l
cast a ray from the middle rather than comparing edges,
Mod4+[ and Mod4+] rotate the orbit, Mod4+= and Mod4+- grow
and shrink the middle one, Mod4+Shift+s throws a window at
the other monitor. See docs/solar.md.
"matrix"    the focused window at 60% of the width on the left, and the
focus history halving away down the right: the one before
this at half the column, the one before that a quarter, and
so on until a slot would be under 100px. What is left over
is stacked in the last slot with a count on it. Order is
Alt+Tab order, so nothing is placed by where it sits in the
tree. No keys of its own — focus is the only input the model
takes. See docs/matrix.md.
"canvas"    every workspace an unbounded plane. Windows sit where you
put them and keep those coordinates; the view pans and
zooms over the top, and zooming out draws them smaller
without resizing any client. Mod4+[ and Mod4+] pan,
Mod4+PageUp/PageDown pan vertically, Mod4+- and Mod4+= zoom,
Mod4+Shift+f fits the plane and Mod4+Home returns to 1:1.
Mod4+left-drag moves a window or pans the desktop,
Mod4+right-drag resizes one.
Zoom stops at 1:1 because past it the compositor would be
enlarging a buffer the client painted smaller. Zooming out
is unrestricted. See docs/canvas.md.
"shell layout.model" switches at runtime; with no argument it cycles.
_layout_extensions: Explicit local scripts keyed by the layout name they register.
Relative paths are resolved beside this config file. Scripts load before
_tiling_mode: How the tiling tree arranges itself. Only meaningful with
"layout": "tiling" — the scrolling strip, the solar layout, the
matrix and the canvas are each their own model.
"manual"        the tree of splits you make. The default.
"master-stack"  first window one side, the rest in a column beside it.
"spiral"        each window halves what is left, turning each time.
"bsp"           the same, cutting along the region's longer side.
"grid"          every window the same size, in rows: 2x2 for four,
3x3 for nine, and fewer rows on a wider screen.
The dynamic modes derive the shape from which windows are open, so
opening one rearranges what is already there — and resize weights reset
when that happens, which is why manual is the default.
"shell layout.mode" switches at runtime; with no argument it cycles.
_focus_crosses_outputs: Whether Mod4+h and Mod4+l — and Mod4+j and Mod4+k — carry focus onto the
next monitor once there is nothing left to reach on this one. True is
sway's behaviour and the default. False stops directional focus at the
edge of the screen, which is worth having on a wide pair of monitors
where the last window on one is a keypress away from focusing something
Asking for a monitor by name is unaffected: a binding on
"shell output.focus right" still crosses. This is about falling off the
end of a screen, not about ever leaving it.
_bar: "visible" always, "hidden" never, or "auto", which reveals the bar
only while Mod4 is held. "auto" is for OLED panels: the bar is the one
part of the screen that never changes, which is what burns in. Mod4+n
still toggles it per output regardless of the mode.
_dark_mode: Which way the session starts. Absent is dark, which is what the shell is
drawn for; false starts light. Mod4+Shift+d flips it at runtime, and
either way the settings portal tells running applications, so GTK, Qt
and Firefox follow rather than staying on whatever they started with.
_decorations: "client" hands the window frame back to the application, which then
draws its own titlebar. Anything else, and leaving the key out, keeps
the frame here — the border the shell draws. xdg-decoration and the KDE
server-decoration manager are answered with the same setting.
_osk: "auto" raises the on-screen keyboard for a focused text-input by
itself, but only once the seat has actually seen a touch device — a
desk with just a keyboard and a mouse never does, so this is the same
as "manual" there. "manual" never raises it on its own, but
Mod4+Shift+k still does. "off" does neither: the chord is bound to
nothing else while this is set, so pressing it does nothing at all,
which is deliberate rather than a keymap left incomplete.
_empty: What the shell draws when a workspace has no windows: the mark, and the
note naming the keys that open something. Worth having the first time
and steadily less so after that. With both off the desktop is empty,
which on an OLED panel is one fewer thing sitting in fixed pixels.
_theme: Colours for the shell, set as CSS custom properties. Any name the
stylesheet reads works; the ones it defines are bg, text, muted, border,
border-focus, bar-bg, bar-border, glow-1, glow-2, bar, radius, tab and
gap. Values are colours or lengths,
not arbitrary CSS. On an OLED panel a true black bg costs no light at
all, which is the only background that does.
_gaps: Space around and between windows, in pixels. `inner` is the gap between
adjacent windows; `outer` is extra space around the edge of the output,
added on top of the inner gap. `smart` drops the inner gap when a
workspace holds a single window, so a lone window does not sit far from
its own screen edge. Absent fields keep the shell's defaults: inner 8,
_border: The frame around a window. `radius` is the corner in pixels, on the
outside of the border; absent keeps the shell's default of 6 and zero
is a square desktop. `width` is how thick the border is; absent keeps
the default of 2 and zero draws none at all. `smart` squares the
corners of a workspace's lone window the way gaps.smart drops its
inner gap; absent follows gaps.smart rather than meaning off, since a
window pushed against the screen edge is the one whose rounded corner
shows wallpaper through it. The first two are read by the
compositor as well as the shell: the client is a surface the
compositor draws, and it crops that surface to the same corner — the
outer radius less the border — or the rounded frame would be hidden
behind a square client. Fullscreen windows keep square corners.
_rules: First matching rule wins. Rich match fields are ANDed; workspace is the
active workspace when the window opens. pseudotile keeps the full tiled
slot while centring a preferred-size client. swallow replaces a matching
parent only through verified native Wayland process ancestry; a child
rule with swallow false opts out. capture false replaces that window
with black in screenshots and screen shares.
_notifications: What a notification sounds like. The compositor holds
org.freedesktop.Notifications itself, so this is the setting mako or
dunst would carry — there is no notification daemon to configure.
`sound_file` is a path, played as given. `sound_name` is a name from
the sound naming specification, resolved against the installed sound
theme (bell, message, complete, dialog-warning); it is ignored when
sound_file is set, because a path always resolves and a name may
resolve to nothing. Absent is silence, deliberately: the freedesktop
theme every distribution installs has no notification event of its
own, so a default here would be one desktop's taste imposed on the
rest. A sender's own sound-file / sound-name hints override these for
its notification, and its suppress-sound hint silences them.
`history` is how many notifications the centre keeps once their popups
have gone — Mod4+Shift+m opens it. 50 unless this says otherwise; 0
keeps no record at all, for a session that would rather not hold a list
of everything that notified it. Memory only: nothing is written to disk,
so a compositor that exits takes the list with it.
_tray: The system tray. On unless this is false, in which case the compositor
claims neither org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher nor a host name and the bar
draws nothing — for a session running waybar's tray, or none at all.
Applied on reload as well as at startup.
icon_theme is the theme an item's icon name is resolved against;
hicolor is searched in any case. An item that ships its own icons and
points at them with IconThemePath is searched there first.
_clipboard_history: How many things the clipboard remembers. Mod4+Shift+v opens the picker.
0 keeps nothing at all, for a session that would rather run cliphist —
or one that does not want a copy of every password that passes through.
Text only, and only the clipboard: the primary selection would mean an
entry for every word dragged over with a mouse.
_bar_widgets: Extra widgets to add to the bar, beyond the modules it ships with.
Leave the key out (or empty) and the bar is exactly as it shipped —
nothing here changes what it draws by default.
{ "type": "battery" }                    charge; click for profiles, suspend, power, reboot
Disk, volume and mic are sampled by the compositor with the rest of the
status, so they show the machine as it is. Weather is fetched by the
shell itself from open-meteo (no key); the location is a place it can
geocode, like a city name. AI credentials come from provider environment
variables; see docs/configuration.md. OpenAI can also sign in when its
widget is clicked. Several of each kind may be listed.
_bar_items: Override the entire right side of the bar with an explicit, ordered list.
Each entry is either a module the bar already draws — a bare string like
an object exactly like a bar_widgets entry. When present (even empty) it
replaces the default modules and any bar_widgets outright — the bar draws
exactly what is listed, in order, and nothing else. That is how a widget
ends up sitting in the middle of the modules rather than after them.
Leave the key out for the default bar.
_outputs: Modes are left to the display by default. max_refresh takes the fastest
refresh rate available at the preferred resolution, which is what a
high-refresh monitor that nominates a 60Hz timing needs. A named mode
may leave the refresh off to match on resolution alone. An exact name
beats "*" whichever order they appear in.
Per-output vrr is off, always, fullscreen, or game-or-video and overrides
the legacy global. mirror names a direct same-GPU source. This first
version requires matching transformed mode and scale; chains are refused.
_input: Per-device libinput settings. '*' applies first; an exact
vendor:product:name key overrides the fields it names. IDs are
four-digit lowercase hex and each identifier is logged on device add.
Unsupported settings are logged and ignored. Applied again on reload.
_gestures: Discrete touchpad gestures use ordinary binding actions. A configured
type and finger count is captured from begin to end; all others are
forwarded to clients unchanged. Swipe threshold is 120 on the dominant
axis; pinch thresholds are 1.2 out and 0.8 in. Cancelled gestures do nothing.
_adaptive_sync: Variable refresh rate. Off by default because it depends on the monitor
and the driver as much as on the compositor, and enabling it where it is
not properly supported causes flicker. Tested against the hardware at
startup and quietly left off if it is refused.
_idle: What to do when nobody is there. Both thresholds are in seconds and
either can be omitted; with neither set there is no policy at all and an
external daemon such as swayidle can own it instead.
The compositor does not draw the lock screen itself — it runs the locker
named here, so that the program drawing it can crash without unlocking
anything. Checked every 5 seconds, so thresholds round up to that.
Idle inhibitors are honoured: a video player holding one keeps the
_lid: What to do when the laptop lid closes. ignore, lock, blank or suspend.
Absent is lock when idle.lock_command is set, otherwise blank. A desktop
has no lid, so the setting never fires. suspend talks to logind.
_keyboard: The keymap, in xkb's own names — the ones setxkbmap takes. Leave the
block out for the built-in default, which is a US layout.
repeat_rate is repeats a second and repeat_delay is how long a key is
held before they start, in milliseconds; absent is 25 and 200.
Read once, at startup: a keymap is set by handing the seat a new
keyboard, and there is no way to change the layout of one that already
exists. A layout xkb refuses is logged by name and the current keymap
kept. Keybindings are matched by keysym, so a chord written here
follows the layout rather than a key's position.
_cursor: The pointer. 'theme' and 'size' are set for the compositor and for
everything it starts, so the arrow over a window and the one over the
'hide_after_ms' takes the image off the screen once the pointer has been
still that long — the arrow parked in the middle of a film. Zero or
omitted is off. Any use of the pointer brings it back at once; typing
does not, because someone writing with the mouse pushed aside is who
_menu: The external menu command, when one is named. Absent is the built-in
launcher: the shell draws it, and the compositor feeds it from the
.desktop directories, filtering on what is typed and starting what is
chosen with an activation token, so the window that appears opens
focused. A binds entry for Mod4+d wins over both.
